findings.prompt_en: Say 'चिड़िया'. Is the first sound short or long — does it take छोटी इ (ि) or बड़ी ई (ी)?
findings.why: acceptable contains ‘चिड़िया’ — the very word the prompt tells the child to say. The question asks short vs long matra; a child who only repeats ‘चिड़िया’, or says ‘बड़ी ई — चिड़िया’, would match and be marked right.

findings.prompt_en: Find the naming words in: 'बच्चे टोकरी में फूल लाए'.
findings.why: acceptable contains ‘तीन शब्द’. The task is to find the nouns (बच्चे, टोकरी, फूल); ‘तीन शब्द’ names none of them and is not an answer.

findings.prompt_en: Finish the doha: 'काल करै सो आज कर, आज करै सो ___'.
findings.why: acceptable contains ‘अभी’ / ‘abhi’. The item is ‘finish the doha’; Kabir's line is ‘आज करै सो अब’ (rhymes with ‘बहुरि करेगा कब’). ‘अभी’ is a paraphrase, not the doha's word, and breaks the rhyme/metre.

findings.prompt_en: {friendF} wrote "प्रिय ___ सारा" in the letter — which spelling of the word for friend is right?
findings.why: prompt_en contains the raw template token ‘{friendF}’ while prompt_hi has the hard-coded name ‘रिया’. Either the English is shown unrendered, or it is rendered with a name that can differ from रिया, so the two languages disagree. Key (मित्र) itself is right.

findings.prompt_en: A student says, ‘मैं अपनी दीदी से प्रेरणा लेती हूँ।’ Retell this about {friendF}, without quoting her. Complete: ‘रिया कहती है कि ___ ___ दीदी से प्रेरणा लेती है।’

acceptable: वह अपनी दीदी से प्रेरणा लेती है
रिया कहती है कि वह अपनी दीदी से प्रेरणा लेती है

findings.why: prompt_en says ‘Retell this about {friendF}’ (raw template token) but both prompts then hard-code ‘रिया कहती है कि …’. If {friendF} renders as any name other than रिया the English contradicts itself and the Hindi. Key (वह अपनी) is right.

findings.prompt_en: In the poem, who brought the new camera?
findings.why: Text-dependent retrieval (poem not in prompt). I guessed पापा; key says चाचा. Could not verify the key without the textbook.

findings.prompt_en: What did Laddoo Dada decide — what should the sweets do, and what should people do?

key.answer: मिठाइयाँ अपने में शक्कर कम करें; लोग जीभ पर नियंत्रण रखें, अति न करें, मेहनत करें और स्वस्थ रहें

findings.mine: सब मिठाइयाँ अपनी-अपनी जगह अच्छी हैं, उन्हें आपस में झगड़ना नहीं चाहिए/मिलकर रहना चाहिए; और लोगों को मिठाई सीमित मात्रा में खानी चाहिए (अनुमान)
findings.why: Text-dependent retrieval (story not in prompt). My guess did not match the key (sweets reduce sugar; people control the tongue, avoid excess). Could not verify the key without the text.

findings.prompt_en: In the end, why did the king take back the punishment?

key.answer: तेनाली ने कहा कि उसके यहाँ सिर तभी मुँड़ाते हैं जब माता-पिता नहीं रहते, और अब राजा ही उसके माता-पिता जैसे हैं — राजा डर गए कि कहीं उन पर विपत्ति न आए

findings.mine: क्योंकि राजा को अपनी ग़लती/सच्चाई समझ आ गई (अनुमान)
findings.why: Text-dependent (Tenali Rama story not in prompt). I gave a generic guess; key is story-specific. Not verified against the text.

findings.prompt_en: The king knew he would not live long. Whom was he looking for?

key.answer: अपने बेटे के लिए एक सलाहकार की

findings.why: Text-dependent. I guessed ‘successor’; key says an advisor for his son. Not verified against the text.

findings.prompt_en: The last line of Madan's poem was made from whose name?

key.answer: धन्नू शाह — जिस आदमी ने उसे राजमहल का रास्ता बताया

findings.mine: (अनुमान) किसी व्यक्ति के नाम से — पाठ के बिना पक्का नहीं
findings.why: Text-dependent; I could not answer without the story. Key: धन्नू शाह (consistent with key of c4-hindi-ch11-t01-i07, which also names धन्नू शाह).

findings.prompt_en: The helpers came one by one. Who came to help right after Bittu?
findings.mine: (story not supplied) unknown — cannot answer without the text
findings.why: Text-dependent; prompt gives no story, I could not answer. Key: कुत्ता (acceptable मोती). Not verified.

findings.prompt_en: Remember the poem: 'Chhota-sa hai ghar mera...' Which line comes next?

key.answer: आँगन में है धूप का डेरा
acceptable: aangan mein hai dhoop ka dera
angan me hai dhup ka dera

findings.mine: (poem's next line not supplied) cannot answer without the text
findings.why: Text-dependent; next line of the poem is not derivable from the prompt. Key: ‘आँगन में है धूप का डेरा’. Not verified.

findings.prompt_en: What do you think the road looks like now, after many years?

key.answer: दोनों तरफ़ बड़े-बड़े बरगद, ठंडी छाया, चिड़ियाँ

findings.mine: open prediction: अब पक्की/चौड़ी, गाड़ियों-दुकानों वाली (या टूटी-फूटी) होगी
findings.why: ‘Predict’ item whose key is story-specific (banyan-lined, shady road). Without the story my open prediction (paved/busy road) does not match; the acceptable list would reject any prediction that is not about trees/shade. Fine only if the story is always told first.

hinglish.why: English ‘drop’ in Devanagari dropped into a class-2 Hindi spelling item; no teacher says ‘बारिश की ड्रॉप’. It is there only to avoid saying बूँद; ‘बारिश में आसमान से जो टपकती है, वह कौन-सी है?’ would do the same job.

level.why: Class 9: ‘रानी खूब लड़ा’ vs ‘रानी खूब लड़ी’ — basic gender agreement, class 2-4 level.
Class 9: write ‘samudra’ in Devanagari — primary-level task (only आख़िरी चट्टान has any difficulty).

Class 8: ‘गौरैया … उड़ गई / गया / गए’ — class 3-4 gender agreement. (Same for DIAG:c8-hindi-ch08-t01-mc-naye-agreement and c8-hindi-ch08-t01-i06, नया/नए/नई.) May be intended as a diagnostic for second-language Hindi learners; flagging in case it is not.

other_notes: No key_wrong found: all 54 MCQ keys match my blind answers, and every non-text-dependent open item agrees in substance.

The 8 disagreements are all items that need the NCERT text and do not supply it (listed as solver_wrong, keys unverified). Other text-dependent items where my answer from memory matched the key: c4 ch02 (snail), c4 ch11 i06/i07, c5 ch03 (चाँद का कुरता), c5 ch04, c6 ch13 (जगदीशचंद्र बसु), c8 ch04 (भारतेंदु), c8 ch06 (एक टोकरी भर मिट्टी), c8 ch09 (गिरिजाकुमार माथुर), c9 ch04 (यतींद्र मिश्र/लता), c9 ch08 (रैदास pairs), c9 ch09 (ख-ग-घ-क).

Internal inconsistency in class 3 ch11 (जादुई पिटारा): retrieval c3-hindi-ch11-t01-i02 keys the things coming out of the box as ‘कहानी, पहेली, गुड़िया, सहेली’ (no खेल in answer or acceptable), while c3-hindi-ch11-t01-i06 and DIAG:c3-hindi-ch11-t01-mc-literal-magic both say ‘कहानियाँ, पहेलियाँ और खेल निकलते हैं’. A child answering ‘खेल’ to i02 would be marked wrong. One of the two needs to follow the poem.

Two-part questions whose acceptable list takes a single part (matcher-dependent, not counted as findings): c3-hindi-ch16-t01-i03 accepts ‘vikram’ or ‘प्रज्ञान’ alone for ‘names of the lander and the rover’ (also cannot detect a swapped assignment); c3-hindi-ch15-t01-i06 accepts ‘utar’ / ‘north’ alone; c7-hindi-ch10-t01-i03 and c7-hindi-ch06-t01-i05 accept any one of the three/four glosses.

Picture-dependent items with no picture in the data: c1-hindi-ch09-t01-i11 (point to आलू), c2-hindi-ch15-t01-i06 (which animals pull the plough). Answerable from general knowledge, but the prompt says ‘look at the picture’.

Hindi spelling/matras in prompts and keys otherwise checked clean (नुक़्ता, चंद्रबिंदु, ज्ञ/क्ष, ड़/ढ़ all consistent); grammar terms (संज्ञा, व्यक्तिवाचक, भाववाचक, प्रत्यय, अनुप्रास, रूपक, उपमा, मानवीकरण, यति, छाप/टेक) are used correctly.
